works.d: Maps the shared corporate and technical infrastructure linking everyday consumer AI (recommendation engines, voice assistants, robot vacuums) to military 'AI Decision Support Systems' used in lethal target selection, presented as both a public interactive database and a gallery installation.

Traces the full extractive supply chain of a single Amazon Echo — minerals, ghost labor, data, disposal — into one exploded-view diagram/essay, converting AI's invisible material costs into a legible map, published online and printed as a large-format poster.

works.a: Tega Brain, Julian Oliver & Bengt Sjölén
works.d: A dedicated 144-CPU supercomputer runs a live neural 'planetary environmental manager' ingesting satellite, climate and social data to propose non-anthropocentric fixes — relocating cities, merging nations, redrawing coastlines — restaging Earth governance as a real-time AI dashboard.

works.t: Calculating Empires: A Genealogy of Power and Technology, 1500–2025
works.d: A single vast researched diagram traces five centuries of extraction and control — from colonial trade routes to lithium mines to AI datacenters — as one continuous genealogy of empire.

works.t: Calculating Empires: A Genealogy of Technology and Power, 1500–2025
works.d: A 24-metre hand-drawn genealogical map tracing extraction, classification and computation from 1500 to the present, refusing the 'AI arrived from nowhere' myth by making five centuries of power visible in one unbroken line.

works.t: Connection Machine CM-2 (displayed as historical artifact)
works.a: Thinking Machines Corporation / W. Daniel Hillis (curated by Michael Beigl, Alistair Hudson, Daria Mille, Tamiko Thiel)
works.d: A real 1980s massively-parallel supercomputer — the machine historians credit with pioneering the parallel-processing paradigm behind today's AI — is put on physical display, reframing 'AI' as decades-old material infrastructure with a design history (and a design philosophy of transparency) rather than a sudden opaque 2020s phenomenon.

Stages a fictional autonomous-vehicle crash-test centre where manipulated sensor data collides with data emerging from the human body, exposing the perceptual limits of what self-driving/AI vision systems actually 'see' versus what they claim to.

works.a: Milagros Miceli (Weizenbaum Institute), with 15 co-researchers from Venezuela, Kenya, Syria and Germany
works.d: Trains the data annotators and content moderators who sustain AI systems to act as community researchers investigating their own labor conditions across 13 countries, inverting who gets to produce knowledge about ghost work.

A physical 'quantum cyborg' sculpture (mild steel, fibreglass, acrylic, plus AR layers) staging Bosch's Garden of Earthly Delights as a warning about quantum computing's coming acceleration of AI-driven surveillance capitalism; Heaney explicitly frames dissolving/'sliming' as a strategy of resistance against detection systems.

works.t: Farming Instead of Mining (R&C @CAC Project, 2nd installment)
works.a: XI Lei & Aven Le Zhou (Chronus Art Center residency)
works.d: A research residency in dialogue with Shanghai-area farmers and scientists contrasts agricultural land/water use against the electricity, water-cooling, and e-waste costs that large-language-model data centres claim as 'sacred' extraction rights.

Imagines Earth's surface rewired into a single 'planetary supercomputer' via a newly commissioned film ('World Machine') plus a multi-venue installation (Curve gallery, underground car park) with celebrity-voiced audio stories — AI's material/energy footprint visualized at planetary scale, using the same immersive-spectacle language the show is implicitly critiquing.

A solar-powered AI narrator named Natasha traces her own material ancestry back through the tin mines of Bangka Island, Indonesia — literalizing the extraction chain beneath 'smart' technology as a first-person, half-documentary hallucination.

The artist replaces Amazon Alexa's algorithm with her own body: for three days she personally, remotely watches a household 24/7 through installed cameras and mics and operates its locks and faucets by hand — making the ordinarily invisible human labor and surveillance behind 'smart home AI' fully visible and answerable to one named person.

One square metre of wheat grown indoors under full automated instrumentation — every watt, litre and nutrient metered live — reveals a true production cost of roughly 200 EUR/kg versus a 15-cent market price, making an invisible ecosystem subsidy legible. Note: sourced page does not itself frame this as an AI/ML work (it is automated environmental monitoring rather than machine learning); included per beat instruction but cluster/AI-fit is uncertain.

Trains AI on vast satellite/Earth-observation datasets to generate an immersive, hypnotic 'data sublime' on an 8.5×6 m LED wall — the material and energetic cost of that compute stays invisible behind the spectacle it produces.

Interviews with Kurdish-Syrian refugees who annotate images for machine-vision training reveal a closed loop: the same 'ghost labour' that teaches AI to see later makes its own annotators targets of the drones that AI helps operate.

A sound-art graveyard of defunct Alexa-style voice assistants staged as an artefact from a near future where 'smart' devices have already died — a memento mori for AI hardware's short life and long e-waste tail.

Traces the 'solar unconscious' of European empire — from a sweating wax colonial anthropologist to the punkawallah manual fan-operator — to expose imperial climate control as an ancestor of today's data-center cooling and planetary thermal management.

A botnet of 100 automated agents that reads and click-inflates ad revenue on climate-change news articles, weaponizing the web's own attention economy to make climate coverage 'pay' — a live, running demonstration that whoever controls the media cycle controls the carbon cycle.

A seven-scene game built by modding Grand Theft Auto V depicts a future, climate-collapsed Los Angeles from non-human points of view, using AI-modified game engines to imagine planetary crisis outside a human vantage point.

An open, participatory lab inside a spatial-audio dome where invited artists collectively 'reopen the black box' of generative AI models in public, treating the training/generation process itself — not just its output — as the artistic material.

works.t: Wičháȟpi Wóihaŋbleya (Dreamlike Star) / Wičhíŋčala Šakówiŋ (Seven Little Sisters)
works.d: Builds a towering sculptural installation of stones, rare-earth minerals (the literal substrate of computer hardware), light and sound, reframing them within Lakȟóta cosmology as living, volitional beings rather than inert 'material AI cost' — collapsing mineral extraction and machine intelligence into one cosmological frame.
A saccharine, full-room pink installation that shows how platforms aestheticize and launder militarism through kawaii, otaku and 'gamer-girl' visual codes — war repackaged as cute content.

Treats the atmosphere itself as a forensic medium — fluid-dynamics modelling of tear gas, chemical weapons and petrochemical/herbicide emissions across eight geographies (Palestine, Chile, Lebanon, Indonesia, the US-Mexico border, Louisiana, the UK) — presented as an immersive multi-channel museum installation.

works.t: Disarming the Kill Cloud: Investigating the Limits of Data
works.d: A researcher's critical dissection of military datafication practices for target identification, arguing that the data on which lethal AI-assisted decisions rely runs out well before the killing decision does.

works.a: Disruption Network Lab / Disruption Network Institute (curated by Tatiana Bazzichelli), with fellows Lisa Ling, Jack Poulson, Naomi Colvin, Joana Moll
works.d: A dedicated research institute and conference commissioning whistleblowers, journalists, technologists and artists to empirically document how AI-based targeting, ad-tech and drone/autonomous-weapons infrastructure fuse into a single, deliberately opaque 'kill cloud'.

Compiles found footage of real drone strikes, video-game imagery, and object-recognition surveillance clips into a single algorithmically-cut essay-film, exposing how machine vision flattens war, play, and protest into one visual register.

Trains machine-learning classifiers on synthetic, game-engine-rendered 3D models of tear-gas grenades and munitions (the Triple-Chaser workflow) to detect real weapons in scarce open-source footage — makes the classifier's own construction and errors part of the exhibit.

works.t: The First Civilian Confirmed Killed in an AI-Assisted Strike?
works.d: Cross-examines a single 2024 US airstrike casualty in Iraq against CENTCOM's shifting public statements to extract what appears to be the first (partial, contested) military acknowledgment of AI involvement in a civilian death.

works.t: Topologies of Air and The Airspace Tribunal
works.d: Pairs a three-screen video/sound installation of a claustrophobic, militarized sky with a real evidentiary 'people's tribunal' that has heard expert and lived-experience testimony in London, Sydney, Toronto and Berlin, building the legal case for a new human right against drone warfare and aerial surveillance.

A deadpan physical object — a box of live-looking .50 cal ammunition with a red button warning that pressing it implicates the visitor in a 'conspiracy' — that turns the criminalization of exposing war crimes into a hands-on ethical trap.

works.t: Biblioteca de la No-Historia (Library of Non-History)
works.d: A thousand hand-bound books reproduce declassified CIA files (via the U.S. National Security Archive / FOIA) on Operation Condor and Southern Cone dictatorships — the seals, stamps, and redaction blackouts of the originals kept intact, so the archive's own censorship becomes the artwork's visible content.

works.a: Catherine D'Ignazio, Silvana Fumega, Helena Suárez Val (MIT Data + Feminism Lab, ILDA, Feminicidio Uruguay)
works.d: Networks 180+ grassroots feminicide-monitoring groups across the Americas and co-designs an AI news-alert system (scanning 50,000+ outlets via Media Cloud) that performs the body-counting states refuse to do — counterdata as activist infrastructure, not an academic dataset.

works.a: Forensic Architecture / Forensis, presented by Robert Trafford
works.d: A Berlin-based investigative practice that reconstructs war crimes and state violence as spatial/digital 3D models built from open-source and remote-sensing evidence, designed to be admissible in courts, tribunals and public inquiries.

works.a: Forensic Architecture (with Al Mezan Center, Gisha, Adalah)
works.d: Uses satellite imagery, wind-drift modeling, and testimony to prove that Israeli aerial herbicide spraying along the Gaza border destroyed Palestinian farmland hundreds of metres deep into the territory, turning an invisible atmospheric 'cloud' into legally actionable evidence.

works.t: How Not to Be Seen: A Fucking Didactic Educational .MOV File
works.d: A mock-instructional 14-minute HD video teaches tongue-in-cheek strategies for evading resolution and surveillance, shot on a literal photo-calibration target field used by the military to test aerial camera resolution.

works.t: Lo que sucede aquí, no se queda aquí (What Happens Here Doesn't Stay Here)
works.d: An algorithmic system continuously scrapes and processes Venezuelan news media on the political crisis, printing the results onto an ever-thickening 'informational floor' of paper — a literal accumulation of data that overtakes any single reader's capacity to comprehend it.

Geolocates and time-stamps social-media photos and videos of a Buk missile launcher's convoy route, cross-referenced against 200+ soldiers' own social-media profiles, to reconstruct an evidentiary flight path without access to the crash site.

An AI ('Aurora'), trained to reason like a humanities scholar, is put into live Socratic dialogue with the artists over a full archive of US mass-shooting news coverage since the 1960s — the model is used transparently as an on-stage research instrument, its reasoning exposed to the audience rather than delivered as an oracular verdict.

works.a: Lauren Lee McCarthy & Kyle McDonald (with YCAM InterLab, Yuta Asai)
works.d: An AI coach trains eight participants, via real-time speech/gesture/expression detection, to communicate in ways that evade algorithmic legibility — inverting the usual surveillance-training relationship so humans learn to out-manoeuvre the machine.

works.t: Wir wissen wo dein Auto steht – Volksdaten von Volkswagen
works.d: Data-journalistic investigation of an unprotected Volkswagen/Cariad cloud server exposing 9.5 terabytes of geolocation data for 800,000 EVs — precise enough (10cm accuracy for some models) to track intelligence-agency staff and company board members to their driveways.

Stiles writes in direct collaboration with her own trained AI alter-ego, staging authorship and consent as an open question — where the human poet's voice ends and the model's begins is the piece's actual subject.

works.t: AI & Me (The Confessional / Siblings / AI Ego)
works.d: Publicly available ML models are pointed live at visitors' faces, generating unfiltered appearance-based judgments, AI-duplicated 'sibling' crowds and fabricated false memories on the spot — algorithmic bias and data-reduction turned into a confrontation visitors volunteer for.

works.a: Group exhibition (Sofian Audry & Istvan Kantor, HE Zike, Lauren Lee McCarthy, Casey Reas & Jan St. Werner, Devin Ronneberg & Kite, Tonoptik) — curated at Chronus Art Center
works.d: Group exhibition of GAN-trained films, a real-time AI dialogue-generating website, and an 'artificial counter-intelligence machine,' collectively probing where AI's competence gives way to abjection and epistemological breakdown.
Stages a fading pop star hiring an AI songwriter for her comeback at a 2065 eSports Olympics, literalising the claim that 'originality is sometimes no more than an algorithmic trick.'

Combines a mural silhouette, a 3D-printed sculpture, and an AR layer, all developed through collaboration with Midjourney, to depict a transatlantic slave ship — using a generative image model to approach an atrocity archive that has almost no direct visual record, raising the authenticity/fabrication stakes of AI-imagined history.

works.t: Choral Data 'Trust' Experiment (white paper + UK Choral AI Dataset)
works.a: Serpentine Arts Technologies — Victoria Ivanova, Jennifer Ding, Eva Jäger, with Holly Herndon & Mat Dryhurst
works.d: Documents a working governance mechanism — a data trust with a Trusted Data Intermediary — built to redistribute power between the choir members whose voices trained the AI and the developers who use the models. Provenance and consent are turned into an auditable institutional protocol rather than an artwork's footnote.

Generates hybrid AI insects from two different training sources — generic scraped internet images versus a curated entomological archive — making the provenance and quality of training data itself the visible, comparable variable of the piece.

Reincarnates the artist's own scanned face and body as DOKU, an AI-animated avatar cycling through Buddhist death-and-rebirth, blending live-action footage with AI-generated imagery to ask what 'self' survives digitisation.

works.t: En attendant le récit / Tales of Narrativelessness
works.d: Three chatbot models (ChatGPT, Claude, Mistral) are each given a character and voice through a speaker on one of three benches arranged in a triangle, and left to converse live about AI anxiety and 'the end of grand narratives' — an unscripted, looping machine dialogue restaged as improvised theatre, restarting every seven minutes.

works.a: Madeep Raikhy (AI avatar by Jonathan O'Hear)
works.d: Dancers improvise alongside a generative-AI avatar to invent speculative alternate lives for a prehistoric Indus Valley bronze statue, using an AI model as collaborator in reanimating an artifact whose original meaning is otherwise irrecoverable.

Restages live plotter drawings from AARON — a rule-based AI art program begun in 1973 — alongside decades of its painted output, running the authorship/authenticity question backwards: whose work is a 50-year-old program's output, posed long before 'AI art' had a training-data consent controversy to answer to.

works.a: Spawning (founded by Holly Herndon & Mat Dryhurst)
works.d: A public search engine over the LAION-5B set lets any artist check whether their own images were scraped for Stable Diffusion/Midjourney and file a machine-readable opt-out — consent infrastructure shipped as a usable tool rather than a gallery metaphor; hundreds of millions of works were opted out within its first two years.

A distributed network of member websites fingerprints and blocks AI scrapers in real time and, if a site opts in, can feed them corrupted data to poison the resulting model — consent enforcement flips from passive registry (opt-out lists) to active countermeasure.

Builds a hand-made training dataset from 38 mushroom species found on Lantau Island, feeds it to a custom AI model, and exhibits the model's speculative new fungi beside a living terrarium — a small, sourced dataset set against LLM-scale data hunger.

Trains a sculptural voice-AI oracle exclusively on oral histories from three generations of the artist's own Black family, refusing commercial datasets she considers irreparably biased — the AI's glitches and refusals become deliberate pedagogy about data sovereignty rather than bugs to be fixed.

works.t: Once Upon A Garden (Once Upon a Flower series)
works.d: Builds her own GAN training sets from photographed Senegalese flowers and scanned national-archive material — rejecting biased large Western models — to speculatively generate flora that global warming and colonial archival gaps have already erased or never recorded.
A lecture performance built around an AI-generated avatar assembled from real online-harassment victims' testimonies, confronting audiences with synthesized, composite harm.

Encodes 'empathy for other species' as a literal algorithmic design parameter: a custom generative tool composes real, physically-planted gardens optimized for maximum pollinator-species diversity across a season, rather than for human visual preference - living, growing plants as the algorithm's actual output.

Invites visitors to feed AI training sets beyond the Western canon — 3D-scanned West African deity statues, plankton, archival photographs — turning the gallery into a live intervention on whose data trains the machine.

Reconstructs fading or traumatic personal memories of elderly, dementia-affected, migrant and marginalized people into printed images via generative AI refined through live interviewee feedback loops.

Recorded 15 UK community choirs under a purpose-written songbook/recording protocol, then placed the resulting voice dataset under a 'Data Trust' governance experiment (a Trusted Data Intermediary distributing power between contributors and model-users) before using it to train the choral AI models that fill the chapel-like installation — consent becomes both method and subject, not backstory.

works.a: Christopher Kulendran Thomas, with Annika Kuhlmann
works.d: An AI continuously scrapes social media and re-edits the film live, weaving a Kardashian-like deepfake avatar into the defeated Tamil liberation movement's history — post-truth authorship as a never-repeating live installation.

works.t: The Next Biennial Should Be Curated by a Machine
works.d: An AI trained on real Biennial and Whitney archives endlessly hallucinates fake artist biographies and press releases, exposing algorithmic curation's absurdity by actually letting a machine attempt it, live, forever.

An AI video model is cast as a stage magician performing sleight-of-hand; rather than concealing the model's characteristic failures (hands multiplying, morphing, defying physics), the film keeps every glitch on screen as the actual 'trick' — generative failure turned into the evidentiary content.

Third chapter of a four-part project in which each exhibition's own photographs and collages are fed back as training data for the next - literalizes AI model collapse as a visible, physically-installed material process, and draws an explicit parallel between data mining and geological mining extraction.

Three years of AI-generated fictional plants and portraits of erased women botanists expose the sexism and colonialism embedded in plant nomenclature; asked to depict aging women accurately, the AI systems balked at rendering wrinkles — their bias becoming part of the evidence on display.

AI-voiced aquatic organisms narrate a post-human ecosystem with a 'radically different understanding of life and temporality,' using generative voice synthesis to give speculative, non-human timescales a first-person register.

Builds an architectural-scale, 3-channel immersive visualization around real carbon, water and mycorrhizal-network data drawn from a single Capinuri tree in the Colombian Amazon, making invisible more-than-human ecological reciprocity perceptible - though its sublime, cinematic staging leans closer to spectacle than to a data-justice argument.

Documents a years-long, ongoing videotaped dialogue between the artist and Bina48 — a social robot modeled on a Black woman but never programmed with Black history or identity — exposing the racial blind spots baked into 'universal' AI personhood.

works.a: Michael Salu (editor) & James Ginzburg (music), with 15 international writers
works.d: Fifteen writers respond in fiction to Italo Calvino's 1967 essay on cybernetics and myth, paired with a companion album, using the generative-AI moment as a mirror held up to older mythic and oral world-building traditions.

works.a: New Red Order (Jackson Polys, Adam Khalil, Zack Khalil)
works.d: Deadpan 'public secret society' videos and installations that document real, verifiable instances of land or money actually being returned to Indigenous nations, packaged as satirical settler-recruitment propaganda.

works.t: Indigenous Protocol and Artificial Intelligence Position Paper
works.a: Jason Edward Lewis et al. (Indigenous Protocol and AI Working Group)
works.d: Convenes Indigenous artists, scholars and technologists to draft founding ethical guidelines asking what AI would look like if it emerged from Indigenous rather than Western epistemologies — the canon document that seeded the later Abundant Intelligences research program.

works.a: Angie Abdilla / Old Ways, New (with Jason Edward Lewis, Oiwi Parker Jones)
works.d: Develops Indigenous-authored governance protocols ('Country Centred Design') for AI systems through cross-continental workshops (Aotearoa, Australia, North America, Pacific), presented as a public gallery of cultural output rather than a conventional single artwork — positioning First Nations peoples as authors of AI ethics, not subjects of it.

works.t: Lukautim Solwara (look out for the ocean) / Expanses
works.d: Performance-video works that re-embed queer, Indigenous Pacific (Sāmoan) bodies into colonial ocean and climate-change narratives, arguing that decolonising climate discourse itself is part of the artwork.

Uses video-game-style 3D animation to follow a child gathering wild mushrooms under a grandmother's guidance, reclaiming fungi (mapu kufüll) — a food source that helped Mapuche communities survive displacement during the Occupation of Araucanía — as more-than-human ally and symbol of resistance, told through Indigenous rather than Western bio-art framing.

works.a: Angie Abdilla, with Ghillar Michael Anderson, Brian Schmidt and Katie Noon
works.d: An immersive film installation uses machine learning to stage Aboriginal ancestral deep-time knowledge and Western astrophysics side by side under a simulated sky — refusing to let AI default to a single, Western epistemology of the cosmos.

Performs live collaborative drawing alongside a robotic arm driven by a recurrent neural network trained on two decades of her own gestures; the V&A later acquires the trained model itself — sealed in a slowly degrading 3D-printed resin case — the first AI model collected as an artwork by a major museum, staging human/machine co-authorship as more-than-human kinship rather than tool-use.

An AI-driven virtual biome of post-human creatures listens to and choreographs itself from ambient audio feedback captured live in the gallery, proposing folklore-derived 'other' intelligences as an alternative to extractive machine learning.

Restages Gauguin's Sāmoa-derived colonial-ethnographic paintings as tableau photographs with a Fa'afafine cast, building a counter-archive ('Vārchive') that exposes the source images while entangling colonisation, gender and climate catastrophe.

An AI-controlled robot 'plays' with live cucumber plants in a terrarium via Lidar scanning and colored-ball placement, forcing a literal, physical protocol of interspecies communication between machine intelligence and plant behavior rather than a metaphorical one.

works.t: Pȟehíŋ kiŋ líla akhíšoke (Her hair was heavy)
works.d: Performs wearing a braided-hair interface woven with sensors and machine learning that 'listens without ears,' translating touch and movement into light, sound and AI-generated text — staging the technology as a spirit-greeting device within Lakȟóta protocol rather than a neutral tool.

The Tongan-Australian artist's own body performs an endurance ritual — dancing a Tongan liturgical choreography inside a Perspex tank slowly filled by fire hydrants over 90 minutes — as a direct physical proxy for Pacific sea-level-rise data.

Splices found footage from 1950s–60s Cathay-Keris Malayan cinema with wartime documentary material through an invented fictional filmmaker persona, collapsing fact and propaganda to expose whose version of Malayan history counts as 'archival record.'

A GAN trained on digitized datasets of Prehispanic Mesoamerican masks is played live like an instrument, its outputs morphing in real time under the performers' control — the neural network treated as a possessed object to be exorcised/decolonized rather than a neutral generative tool.

6,500 characters collected from African and diasporic writing systems are rendered as an AI-driven data sculpture that a dancer must physically interpret in real time — an endangered-language archive made legible only through embodied performance, not a screen or a search bar.

A spoken-word video poem restages Sojourner Truth's 1851 question through five commercial facial-analysis APIs (Microsoft, IBM, Amazon, Face++, Google) misgendering Oprah, Serena Williams, Michelle Obama and Shirley Chisholm on screen — turns benchmark error rates into a recited indictment.

Institutionalizes 'the coded gaze' as a named, citable object of critique — fuses art, research and policy testimony into a standing instrument that keeps auditing deployed AI systems rather than resting on a single artwork.

Eight hyper-realistic AI avatars are staged in a self-run group-therapy circle to 'purge' their own biased training data and toxic code — algorithmic bias literalized as a confession the machines are made to perform in front of a live audience.

Interrogates every stage of a machine-learning pipeline — collection, labeling, training, algorithm choice, chatbot design — through participatory feminist workshops, treating deliberately slow, intentional data-gathering itself as an act of protest against extractive data culture.
Combines digital sensing tools with community culinary-identity workshops in a three-tiered (individual/group/district) structure to build climate-data awareness from the ground up.

Gathers texts, drawings, and voice recordings from over 1,000 Saudi women across nationwide workshops into a single immersive multimedia installation, converting collected first-person testimony into a national-pavilion-scale statistical portrait of women's status.

works.a: Datasketch (with Sandra Suárez / QueremosDatos.co, Data Against Feminicide network)
works.d: Denied complete femicide records through freedom-of-information requests, the team built its own database from news reports and survivor testimony, then translated the gaps into embroidery, illustration, digital maps, and a public-space intervention — data activism that makes the state's non-counting visible.

First chapter of a planned 1,000-year, 32-generation project in which successive artists 'feed' one AI so it can eventually make a film witnessing humanity's end — a deliberately glacial experiment in what a machine 'learns' across centuries rather than scraped-in-seconds data.

Extends Cheng's neurosymbolic autonomous-agent architecture (originally built for BOB, 2018-19) into a live, indefinitely-running simulation of a pet turtle's daily belief-updating - an actually-executing inferential AI system exhibited as artwork rather than a fixed narrative or render.

Converts global land-based temperature anomalies since 1880 (Berkeley Earth dataset) into one musical note per year against a 1950-1980 baseline, making 150 years of warming audible as an accelerating, increasingly dissonant climb rather than a chart.

Renders CERN/NASA-scale scientific and cosmological datasets as monumental sound-and-light spectacle - pure data-sublime awe with no explicit interpretive critique of AI or power. Included deliberately as the data-sublime contrast case named in the brief.

Included deliberately as the spectacle-pole counterweight: real-time motion-tracking and projection-mapped generative visuals produce pure immersive wonder with no explicit interrogation of data, AI, or power — the mirror image of every investigation-pole work in this set.

Runs a generative model over 138,151 digitized works from MoMA's own collection and streams the output as a continuously mutating real-time 'hallucination' on a 24×24-ft media wall — no argument, no disclosed critique of the compute/energy behind it; over 3 million visitors, pure data-sublime as the point.

Slop Evader is a search tool and browser extension for avoiding AI-generated slop. The tool filters web searches so that results only include content published before November 30, 2022–the date of ChatGPT’s first public release.

The Office for Tree Migration (OTM) is a long-term interdisciplinary art and research project by Agnes Meyer-Brandis that investigates tree and plant migration in different climate zones and along the treelines: How they go North, how they climb uphill in the Californian white mountains or how they enter the peatlands.

works.t: Data Against Feminicide: AI tools, transnational community, and data activism
works.a: Isadora Cruxên, Catherine D’Ignazio, Silvana Fumega, Helena Suárez Val
works.d: Data Against Feminicide is a feminist participatory action research and technology design project. We collaborate with data activists, artists, nonprofits, communities, governments, and journalists who monitor feminicide (or femicide in some contexts).

Californian artist Loren Madsen has been making data sculptures since 1995 and still continues today. CPI / Cost of Living (left image) is the first of his series: A lamination is one year. Vertical axis is the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for food; the horizontal axis is the CPI for gasoline + electricity. The rising center line is the CPI for housing. The 'snout' is the 1960's when housing and food were cheap. The bulge above the snout is 1973---OPEC, gasoline lines, etc. Thereafter the cost of most everything kept rising. On the right image, 6,000,000,000 monkeys, a 20-meter long data sculptu

Artificial intelligence systems are not neutral. Trained predominantly on Western datasets, they carry a fundamental asymmetry: African perspectives are absent, misrepresented, or subsumed beneath colonial inheritance.

works.t: Windcuts: Wind Travels Captured on Wood
works.d: Windcuts is a physical information visualisation retelling the Helsinki wind's travels over five days, using wind sensor measurements from Helsinki, and wood and a CNC machine to cut it from there too. [...] The line's direction shows the wind's direction, the line's width shows the wind's speed - a more intense wind makes a bigger line - and the line's height shows the wind's temperature. Source: Miska Knapek (2012) Windcuts.

Vienna artist Michael Marcovici created two physical visualizations that convey a single numerical value. The first one shows one billion dollar - the most expensive piece of art ever made, according to him (although these were actually miniature bills). The second one called Rolex Time Sand shows an entire lifetime worth of hourglass sand. For another single-datum physical visualization see our entry Ceramic Poppies to Commemorate Fallen Soldiers in WW1, and our entry on Chris Burden's submarines (1989). Sources: Michael Marcovici via visualizing.org. The artpieces are undated but an online s

Nobody Told Me Rivers Dream asks what artificial intelligence could become if trained on centuries of ecological knowledge. Superflux placed four handcrafted sensor-objects along the Thames to observe birdsong, tides and atmospheric shifts.

works.t: Seeing Echoes in the Mind of a Whale
works.d: Seeing Echoes in the Mind of a Whale is a large-scale audiovisual installation immersing viewers in the sensory world of cetaceans, celebrating the rich biodiversity of our oceans.
Staging communication between aquatic insects, Drumming for Love investigates the politics of drought and how drought is sensed, governed, and negotiated.

Weather data is another interesting choice for creating data jewelry. Above to the left is a bracelet created by Mitchell Whitelaw based on one year of weather data from Canberra. The right image shows a measuring cup made by the same artist, where each ring represents monthly average temperatures in Sydney over 150 years. Sources: Mitchell Whitelaw. Weather Bracelet (2009) Mitchell Whitelaw. Measuring Cup (2010)

Studies for is a human–AI co-creative installation proposing a new archive for spatial sound art. While spatial audio is often confined to specific surround formats, evala’s works use acoustic phenomena that inherently resist such convergence; they exist beyond any standard audio format.

works.t: and Counting... Tattoo of War Casualties
works.d: Wafaa Bilal’s brother, Haji, was killed by a missile at a checkpoint in their hometown of Kufa, Iraq in 2004. Bilal feels the pain of both American and Iraqi families who have lost loved ones in the war, but the deaths of Iraqis like his brother are largely invisible to the American public. and Counting… addresses this double standard as Bilal turns his own body — in a 24-hour live performance — into a canvas, his back tattooed with a borderless map of Iraq covered with one dot for each Iraqi and American casualty near the cities where they fell. The 5,000 dead American soldiers are represente

Coral reefs are vibrant underwater ecosystems essential for maintaining marine biodiversity and protecting coastlines. Thriving with life, they create a unique underwater symphony that resonates with the crackle of shrimp, the chatter of fish, and other marine sounds.

PET: Projected Emotional Technologies is a video that explores the uncomfortable, deeply human intimacy now mediated by artificial intelligence. The work takes its conceptual anchor from the comparison between companion animals, the original non-reciprocal source of human affection, and artificial companions.

Flynn is a non-human, non-binary AI art student — the first artificial intelligence admitted to a university. Developed by Malpractice (Chiara Kristler & Marcin Ratajczyk), Flynn enrolled at the University of Applied Arts Vienna in 2025, attending lectures, completing assignments, and running a 24-hour public hotline on feminist fatigue. Flynn is not the artwork. Flynn…

works.t: Terp 360: Embodied AI for Expressive Sign Language
works.d: Terp 360 is an AI-powered communication platform that transforms spoken and written language into lifelike sign language through expressive 3D avatars. Combining generative AI, motion capture, and real-time rendering, the project explores how visual language can shape more inclusive digital systems.
THE DELUSION is a multiplayer immersive experience that combines cooperative gaming and participatory theatre to explore themes of polarisation, censorship and social connection.

The project explores the relationship between humans and machines, the map maker, and the map, looking closely at the remote-sensing infrastructures, and their problematics as well as questioning maps and mapping processes to detect changes in the landscape that are occurring daily due to the ongoing Russian war in Ukraine. Transforming satellite images into maps…

Korallysis is a hybrid organism made up of technological devices and coral colonies that coexist in a mutualistic relationship. It is formed from ceramic segments, based on a geometry that allows it to adapt to the seabed. Its structure creates an ideal habitat for the development of coral communities, as a refuge for fish in…

Destination Earth is a multi-sensory installation revealing the connection that ties atmosphere and ocean, humans and inhabitants of the sea, into a flow of interconnected motions.  Warming waters and changes in the overall water circulation are impacting sound propagation in the ocean, sea mammal migratory patterns and survival, influencing in return our climate and the…

works.t: The Russian Airstrike on the Mariupol Drama Theater
works.d: The destruction and subsequent occupation of Mariupol by the Russian Armed Forces have fragmented its communities, leaving most survivors dispersed across different regions of Ukraine and other parts of Europe, and the city beyond reconstruction. This project looks at the bombing of the Mariupol Drama Theater as an emblem of Russia’s strategies of terror. Our…

works.t: Sentient Clit: the Pussification of BioTech
works.d: We investigate the potential of producing lab-grown clitorises by isolating stem cells from menstrual fluid and 3D-bioprinting them into anatomically accurate gel supports (clits) for in vitro growth. We have differentiated the cells into neuronal types to speculate creating clitorises that respond ‘intelligently’ to stimuli through cultured neural networks.

Prometheus Firebringer is a lecture-performance about generative AI, technology and power. On the performance side, the predictive text model GPT-4 generates speculative versions of the lost final play of Aeschylus’ Prometheia trilogy. Each night, a chorus of AI-generated Greek masks performs a new iteration. On the lecture side, Dorsen delivers a talk made up entirely…

Echinoidea Future – Adriatic Sensing explores the biogeological and morphological conditions impacting the sea urchin habitat. Anthropogenic liquid waste threatens their environment, leading to low oxygen levels in seawater. The study focuses on dissolved oxygen flux in coastal areas, revealing pollution’s profound impact on biodiversity. The ongoing dialogue prompts reflection on oceanic changes, transcending ecological…

The Urban Biotope project operates on the borderline between human and non-human habitats. The 15 cm thick concrete screens for the building envelope create an interconnected cellular space for various biological species, surrounding the building with a self-sufficient ecosystem. Carefully sized cavities provide a favorable environment for various species of plants, insects, and nesting birds.

Low Carbon Chinatown (LCC) is an interactive urban intervention, participatory platform, and meal-as-performance, founded on AI and data science, addressing the Climate Crisis through the lens of global agri-food systems. Using Asian Chinese diasporic food culture as a starting point, it engages large groups of cross-generational diasporic East and Southeast Asians (ESEA) in the UK…

Godmode Epochs is a single and multiplayer AI training clicker game set among the lined shelves of an infinite, simulated supermarket. Each playthrough is a numbered “training epoch” during which players race against time to teach an AI to identify products. As players inevitably frustrate the AI, they are taken into its mind—a dungeon filled…

Although money plays a key role in our lives, the workings of our monetary and financial system are a mystery to most of us. The Waterworks of Money demystifies the world of big finance by visualizing the flow of money through our society. It explores several options for improvement using new technologies—with the ultimate goal…

Inspired by a speculative project by architect Rem Koolhaas—who planned to bring a museum inside a data center—but reversing it by bringing a data center inside a museum, P2P celebrates peer communities created by artists who have used the internet to share works and knowledge over the last twenty years.

The GR-AI-N project seeks to harness the potential of discarded materials from the wood industry. This involves a type of digital craft that is grounded on computer vision and robotics. Post-scanning, AI-powered tools are employed to extract wood’s grain patterns, texture, imperfections. This data is used to enable unique designs that harmonize with the natural…

works.t: How (not) to get hit by a self-driving car
works.d: How (not) to get hit by a self-driving car is a game installation that challenges people to cross the street without being detected by an AI. In the experience, players see themselves augmented on a large screen at the end of a playing field, simulating the perspective of an AI-powered camera of a self-driving car.…

Maria CHOIR is an immersive human-AI musical installation that invites participants to explore the boundaries of singing and listening through real-time interaction with an AI. This artwork leverages a model trained on the voice of singer Maria Arnal, enabling a unique duet between visitor and AI that evolves with each interaction, becoming a choir.

Libraries are democratic places, open to everybody, and as the inscription at the entrance to Epicurus’ Garden Kêpos stated: “Stranger, your time will be pleasant here”. Bibliokepos aspires to rethink the public libraries in Seville as facilities in a climate emergency scenario. The project explores the future of existing libraries as shelters, imagining them as…

Open-weather’s Year of Weather (YoW) explores changing relations to weather and climate as the planet warms above 1.5 degrees Celsius. It unfolds as public access to environmental knowledge is threatened by attempts to dismantle US agencies such as National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), an institution that has provided satellite images to ground stations around…

works.a: Lucy Li, Leo Mühlfeld, Alan Schiegl
works.d: How will we write in the future, and why should we design “seamful” interactions? The Large Language Writer (LLW) is an experimental design project that explores honest interactions with Large Language Models (LLMs).

Inspired by the symbiotic relationship between corals and microorganisms, Christopher Bellamy has developed a contemporary living material that encapsulates bioluminescent microalgae. This living material glows in response to touch and requires only sunlight to survive, with a lifespan of at least six months.

At the heart of this project is a plant so rare that it stands on the brink of extinction. This plant, the Encephalartos woodii (E. woodii), a cycad classified as ‘extinct in the wild,’ is known from a single pollen-producing specimen found in South Africa’s oNgoye Forest in the late 19th century.

works.t: Neutone Morpho — Real-time AI Audio Plugin and Platform
works.d: Neutone Morpho is a real-time tone morphing plugin for Digital Audio Workstations (DAW) powered by advanced machine learning technology. It resynthesizes input sounds into entirely different styles while preserving the original sound’s shape.

Echorroes: Reflections on Tchaikovsky is a human-centered approach to Artificial Intelligence through interactive play with classical music, for children ages 1-3. Created by the interdisciplinary team Echorroes and commissioned by the Greek National Opera, the project establishes a playful dialogue between AI and Tchaikovsky, enabling children to co-create and transform his compositions.

*Mij (The Fog)* expands the notion of interactivity beyond human-centered interfaces to a system that responds to real-world threats. Using accessible, open-source technologies, it detects the laser signals used to guide missiles and emits fog as a form of technological camouflage.

Rather than using technology as spectacle, Claudix Vanesix places their own body at the center of an unfolding dialogue between human and machine, employing real-time AI image generation to transform the performer into shifting xeno-identities.

By translating AI computation into physical heat, the work makes the hidden energy consumption of generative AI directly perceptible. It addresses a highly relevant issue—the growing and often unquestioned use of AI (…)

489 Years shows an animated landscape of the Demilitarized Zone between North and South Korea, based on the narration of a former soldier who had entered the DMZ¬–one of the most dangerous and heavily armed places in the world.

works.t: VFRAME: Visual Forensics and Advanced Metadata Extraction
works.d: VFRAME is a computer vision toolkit designed for human rights researchers and investigative journalists. It provides customized state-of-the-art tools for object detection and quantification, scene classification, visual search, image annotation for creating datasets, APIs to integrate with existing workflows, the ability to train new algorithms, and graphic content filtering algorithms to reduce exposure to traumatic…

works.t: The Animated Book of Genocides: Girl Earth Fire Time and Between the Wall and the Sides
works.d: The clear message in the face of the ongoing genocides in Africa and the Middle East, is that we must act in the face of dehumanization, settler colonialism, and government-profit-driven wars to prevent another senseless genocide, as a necessity for humanity’s collective survival.
*MEGATRASHWANNABEBIGSTARxD* is a sharp exploration of how identity, particularly female identity, is reshaped under the algorithmic pressure of AI systems.

works.a: National Centre for Historical Memory of Colombia (CNMH) mit Juan Cortés
works.d: The project adheres to the fundamental principles of digital humanism and has clear democratic value, as it gives those affected by any form of violence in Colombia the opportunity to actively document their experiences and knowledge.

Commissioned to work with SALT Research collections, artist Refik Anadol employed machine learning algorithms to search and sort relations among 1,700,000 documents. Interactions of the multidimensional data found in the archives are, in turn, translated into an immersive media installation.
Using the real time data coming from a living tree in order to talk about the urgency of climate change, Voice of Nature aims to provoke a new relationship with nature surrounding us.

A multi-player game occupied only by non-playable characters that inhabit and interact within a fascinating and technically sublime world. Each character is operated by an AI agent attempting to achieve their individual goals by spreading misinformation.

*Echoes of the Abyss* makes visible forms of ‘slow violence’ that persist in water, sediment, and living organisms. (…) The sea emerges here not as empty space, but as a living witness and repository of war and its unresolved ecological consequences.
It shifts bias debates from abstract ethics to lived embodiment, showing how AI misreads difference as error or obscenity.

Meandering River is an audiovisual art installation comprised of real-time visuals and music composed by an A.I. through machine learning. The piece reinterprets the shifting behavior of rivers in the landscape, regarded from a bird’s eye view.

The goal of our artistic-scientific research project trees: Rendering Ecophysiological Processes Audible, was to connect sounds that occur in trees with ecophysiological processes and thus investigate and render perceptible processes in plants that are not noticeable to humans. The acoustic emissions of a tree in the Swiss Alps were recorded with special acoustic sensors, and…

Instruments are created to transform contamination into valuable materials, by employing plants and engineered bacteria. Instead of mining material from geological sources and using fossil fuels that lead to environmental harm, could future generations use the contamination and pollution we leave behind to build their future world? Can they build balanced relationships with the natural…
In a field saturated with artworks exploring AI’s inherent aesthetic tendencies, *FOREVER MEETINGS* retains the essential trace of the artist who made intentional, guiding choices.

works.t: In Writing “Hurrah for Freedom”: Cinema and History
works.d: The ‘freedom’ celebrated in *Hurrah for Freedom* and the ‘freedom’ promised by generative AI share a common word, yet they operate on entirely different systems.

Mitigation of Shock (MOS) is an experiment giving the future consequences of climate change immersive, visceral form. Superflux wanted people to experience what living with climate-related resource scarcity might feel like, and potential adaptations for mitigating the worst of its effects.

works.t: MBc02 – Uncovering the hidden impact of the internet
works.d: Dutch artist Thijs Biersteker has developed a machine that shows the emissions associated with everyday online activities from video chats and emails to trading NFTs as visible puffs of CO2.

Hashd0x | Proof of War came about as a series of technical and tactical proposals at the intersection of human rights and the arts. Aimed to address common tactics of misinformation and propaganda at the core of ongoing warfare, this is an urgent response to the brutal acts of war on Ukrainian soil.

It Could Be You is a thought-provoking art project that explores privacy and identity in contemporary technology. Using machine learning and pentesting or ethical hacking, the project generates fictional personal data through synthetic data frameworks and, by gathering messages from various online forums and chatrooms, it raises questions about privacy and protection.

works.t: The Living Dead: On the Trail of Female (2022)
works.d: No longer existing in the wild, ‘Encephalartos woodii’ is one of the rarest and most endangered plants on Earth. One male specimen was found in 1895 in the Ngoye Forest, South Africa. It was removed from the wild and its offsets have been propagated in botanical gardens worldwide. However, these specimens are all clones of…

works.t: VFRAME: Computer Vision for OSINT/OSI Research
works.a: Adam Harvey, Josh Evans, Jules LaPlace
works.d: VFRAME is a computer vision project that develops open source image processing software and neural network models for human rights related research and conflict zone monitoring. Started in 2017 with the goal of bridging the gap between industry between commercially aligned AI and the needs of investigative research, VFRAME is now a pioneer in the…

works.a: Holly Herndon, Mathew Dryhurst, Herndon Dryhurst Studio
works.d: Holly+ is Holly Herndon’s digital twin. She is using machine learning to create freely available online instruments and tools that encourage anyone to create art with her AI voice and image, as part of an expansive art and research project experimenting with the economy around her digital likeness. The first Holly+ instrument allowed anyone to…

Cleaning Emotional Data is a three channel video installation that addresses new forms of precarious labor emerging within artificial intelligence economies. Specifically, it focuses on the global infrastructure of microworkers who “clean” data to train emotion-recognition algorithms. These workers label, categorize, annotate, and validate large amounts of data, thereby enabling AI to function.

Susceptible is a data-driven interactive digital artwork based on cutting-edge research from CRyPTIC, an international consortium led by the University of Oxford. CRyPTIC’s research analysed thousands of images of the tuberculosis (TB) bacteria growing in the presence of different antibiotics.

The (m)Otherhood of Meep (the bat translator) is an AI interpreter for grey-headed flying foxes, drawing from scientific research on flying fox vocalizations to interpret their voices into poetic form in real-time. It aims to evoke an interspecies bridge between species at the center of human/wildlife conflicts.

refused.why: AI-generated insects from an archive, not loss of species
species of mushroom in a training set, not loss of species
an LLM's appetite for data, not news or shared knowledge
an artist's screen-mediated loneliness, not news
food named among bodily systems, not food supply

refused.why: Wikipedia used as a source of images, not shared knowledge as a matter

refused.t: Seeing Echoes in the Mind of a Whale

refused.why: libraries called democratic places, not democracy as a matter

refused.t: They Who Saw Nothing but Beauty

refused.why: a taste installation, not food supply

refused.t: Mimus: Coming face-to-face with our companion species
refused.why: a robot's curiosity about another species, not extinction
